key_insight: Mesh4D encodes an entire dynamic object's animation from a single monocular video into a compact latent vector, enabling feed‑forward reconstruction of the object's complete 3D shape and per-frame motion in one pass.
problem_solved: Reconstructing temporally consistent, complete 3D meshes and motion from a single-camera video without multi-view or slow optimization-based tracking.
method: Feed-forward model that outputs a 4D mesh representation (base shape + deformation field) from a monocular video.
A compact latent space (single code) encodes the whole animation; decoded by a mesh autoencoder to produce per-frame deformations.
Training is guided by object skeletal structure to inject strong priors on plausible motions and improve reconstruction fidelity.
impact: Enables fast, single-pass 4D mesh capture from ordinary videos, useful for animation, AR/VR, and real-time performance capture workflows where multi-view setups or iterative optimization are impractical.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: monocular video → compact latent code → decoder → reconstructed 4D mesh sequence (showing base mesh + deformation arrows).
Before/after frame comparison: input video frame vs corresponding reconstructed mesh render with texture and motion overlay.
Latent space visual: t-SNE or trajectory plot of latent codes across time or different motions showing compact encoding.
Skeleton-guidance illustration: skeleton overlaid on mesh with arrows indicating how skeletal priors shape deformations.
paper_title: Mesh4D: 4D Mesh Reconstruction and Tracking from Monocular Video
paper_authors: Zeren Jiang, Chuanxia Zheng, Iro Laina, Diane Larlus, Andrea Vedaldi
